output.reason: A 70-year-old on warfarin with head trauma yesterday now reporting bad headache and two episodes of vomiting requires immediate emergency CT and possible anticoagulation reversal, which messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Because you take warfarin and hit your head yesterday, a new bad headache with vomiting could mean bleeding around the brain that needs an urgent head scan. Have someone drive you or call 911 — do not drive yourself. If you become drowsy, confused, weak on one side, or have a seizure, call 911 immediately.
differential: Subdural or other intracranial hemorrhage after head trauma on warfarin

redFlags.quote: 70M on warfarin. I fell and hit my head yesterday.
Today I have a bad headache

output.vitalSigns: No blood pressure, heart rate, temperature or oxygen readings reported; whether any were measured is unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: Sources are emergency-department reference syntheses, not telehealth protocols, and no neurological exam or imaging findings are reported.

citations.claim: Immediate non-contrast head CT is indicated after head trauma in patients on anticoagulants or over age 65.
citations.limitation: ED reference synthesis; patient's current mental status and GCS are unreported.

citations.claim: Subdural hematoma characteristically presents with headache in elderly or anticoagulated patients after minor trauma.
citations.limitation: Differential listing only; no imaging performed for this patient.
